highlights.title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
highlights.summary: In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.
body: Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter’s moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a “commemorative phonograph record,” in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whomever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.

About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson. While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs’ overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago.

“So much has been written about the contents of the record —the message in the bottle, so to speak—whereas I was more interested in the hardware, the bottle itself, because so very little is known about that,” Swanson, former chief historian for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston and founding editor of “Quest: The History of Spaceflight Quarterly,” said in an interview.

highlights.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
highlights.summary: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI…
body: “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”

In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It says its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture new scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.

highlights.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
highlights.summary: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry.
body: The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.

Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.
There also appears to be a clear frontrunner. “I would put money on Netflix to win – they will pay whatever it takes,” one experienced media rights buyer told the Guardian.

highlights.title: Clair Obscur's narrative lead has left developer Sandfall Interactive after "wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition"
highlights.summary: Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year.
body: "No, I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she told Gamesbeat when asked if she's still with the company. "We've parted ways." As to what Svedberg-Yen is doing next, she offered a cryptic answer, including talk of writing "my own projects, my own stories". She also discussed another project she's set her sights on: establishing a fund to help mentor and grow a new generation of video game narrative designers.

"One of the initiatives I want to build is a narrative investment fund to focus on narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers," she explained, noting her background working in finance and how that dovetails nicely with her more recent experience as a narrative lead. "This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face. To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors."

highlights.title: Minister criticises media for 'amplifying' Russell Brand's prison message
highlights.summary: Lucy Powell says outlets shouldn't have played a clip of a message read by the jailed rapist's wife.
body: Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell has criticised media organisations for broadcasting a message from the wife of jailed rapist Russell Brand on his behalf.

Laura Brand read out the message on the disgraced comedian's YouTube channel on Sunday, in which he said he was not guilty of the offences for which he is serving a 10-and-a-half year prison sentence.
The message has prompted an official investigation into whether Brand broke prison rules.

The clip of Laura Brand has been played on outlets including BBC Radio 4's Today programme, ITV's This Morning, Sky News, LBC and the News Agents podcast. On Wednesday, Education Secretary Powell said the media should not have "amplified" his words.

highlights.title: David Beckham's perfume, Poundland – and a mighty, mighty stink | Arwa Mahdawi
highlights.summary: The Beckhams have made an art of monetising their every move. But apparently there are limits to where they’re prepared to sell their wares. Thoughts and half-price prayers with Poundland, please. The discount chain has been on the verge of collapse for a while, and its future looks bleak.
body: Not literally, by the way: I suppose I should spell that out since we’re dealing with a litigious billionaire. I did not mean to imply or cause a reasonable person to infer that Sir David is standing on Brixton high street kicking a Poundland. Rather, DB Ventures, the licensor of the David Beckham brand, is causing a bit of a stink about the fact that the football legend’s fragrance range was found on sale in the discount store as well as at other purveyors of budget goods. It is now suing the perfume company, Coty, which it further accuses of under reporting sales, for $41m (£31m).

“DB Ventures … ensures that all of its brand licensing partnerships maintain the lifestyle and luxury image of the brand that Sir David has carefully cultivated for decades,” court filings stated. “Imagine, then, the shock and dismay experienced when DB Ventures discovered that David Beckham products were being offered for sale in a gas station. How could this possibly have happened? Desperation and greed.” Coty has denied that it had ever sold the fragrances in Poundland.

highlights.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe is now one light-day away
highlights.summary: After traveling through the void of space for 49 years, Voyager 1 has hit a momentous milestone: the spacecraft is now officially one light-day away from Earth, which is, as NASA put it, "very, very far." The probe crossed the milepost on Wednesday at 5:16AM ET, and is now 16.094 billion miles away…
body: It’s taken Voyager 1 almost 50 years to journey further from Earth than light can travel in 24 hours.

It’s the furthest that any human-made object has ever traveled, and Voyager 1’s journey isn’t over yet. It’s been heading towards a star called Gliese 445 in the Ursa Minor constellation since completing its primary objectives to conduct flybys of Jupiter and Saturn in 1980. That star is 17 light-years away, meaning Voyager 1 won’t pass by it for around 40,000 years, despite traveling at nearly 38,000 miles per hour.

The light-day milestone is a remarkable feat alone, but especially so when you consider that Voyager 1 is still operational. NASA has done well to keep it functioning, and it can continue to send back readings on plasma waves, magnetic fields, and space-bound particles, though it now takes radio signals an entire day to travel between Earth and the spacecraft. Voyager 2, which launched 16 days before its twin, is also expected to reach a distance of one light-day away from Earth, but not until 2035.

highlights.title: India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed U.S. robotics companies the data they need
highlights.summary: Founded in February, Humyn Labs competes with startups including Mecka AI and XDOF, with about 90% of its revenue coming from the U.S.
body: As demand grows for real-world data to train robots, India’s Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to help U.S. AI and robotics companies build models that can operate in physical environments.

The funding comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finance’s Finserv Intelligence and Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading. It also includes $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton Growth Debt Fund II, with participation from Trifecta Capital.

Companies around the world are trying to build robots capable of performing everyday human tasks, but getting enough quality data to train them remains difficult. Startups including Mecka AI, XDOF, and MicroAGI are already tackling the problem by collecting real-world data for robotics training. Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs aims to compete with them.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Hits 99 on Metacritic, Crowned Best Game Ever in Wave of Rave Reviews
highlights.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has displaced the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the best video game of all time according to review aggregation site Metacritic. Its Metascore of 99 matches Nintendo's 1998 masterpiece, but is presumably a few decimal points higher behind the scenes.
body: It is rated even more highly than Rockstar's last two monoliths, Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, which both earned Metascores of 97. It's a similar story on OpenCritic, where GTA 6 has a rating of 98.
Reviewers are universally bowled over by the scale, ambition, and artistry of Rockstar Games' magnum opus, which they have hailed in a near-unbroken string of five-star, 10/10 reviews.

IGN's Luke Reilly called GTA 6 "one of the most impressive games ever made" in his 10/10 review, and called it "Unprecedented. Unbelievable. Unmissable." Like many reviewers, Reilly noted how the latest GTA had inherited the sophistication and maturity of Red Dead Redemption 2 as well as the anarchic spirit of its predecessors. "As optimistic as I was about a new GTA built in the wake of everything Rockstar learnt from the majestic Red Dead Redemption 2, I was simply not ready for just how much richer, deeper, and more satisfying Grand Theft Auto 6 has proven to be," Reilly wrote.

highlights.title: Marrakech’s Atlas Workshops Takes Victory Lap as Industry Event Celebrates Cannes, Venice Triumphs
highlights.summary: Around this time one year ago, Hédi Zardi, head of the Marrakech Film Festival’s Atlas Programs, was approached by a young filmmaker with an urgent request. The director, who had a feature film in development at the industry event, was just putting the finishing touches on a short film.
body: “Everything is possible,” Zardi insists, with a wave-of-the-hand nonchalance that undersells the work he and his team do to achieve the best possible outcome for every film entrusted into their hands. It’s a philosophy he describes as “curat[ing] each moment” and attempting — through a combination of one-on-one meetings, casual lunches and other events — to “build connections to see what happens.”

For Shaden Safieddine Tazi — the young Moroccan Lebanese director who came to Zardi with her urgent appeal — that approach resulted in a trip to Venice, where her short “A Few Moments of Happiness” was selected for the festival’s Horizons section, winning the award for best short film.

It’s been just eight years since the Marrakech Film Festival introduced its industry program, Atlas Workshops, which was conceived as a springboard for filmmakers from Africa and the Arab world. (It’s now one of several sections joined under the Atlas Programs banner.) This year’s event runs Nov. 22 – 26.

highlights.title: Get vaccinated, don’t vape – and moisturise liberally! 10 doctors on how to avoid and treat winter ailments
highlights.summary: The nights are drawing in, the temperature is dropping, festive overindulgence is on the horizon and it’s easy to get run down. Here’s some expert advice to help you safely through the season.
body: Winter can be a challenging time, with bad weather, dark evenings, horrible bugs circulating, plus plenty of opportunities for overindulging. How can we avoid getting run down? Doctors share their tips for surviving the season, from saunas to screen blockers, light boxes to apples.

“I make sure I have my flu vaccine as early as I can. I had influenza B last year and it took me three months to recover. The vaccine has been shown to be more effective if you have a healthy gut microbiome, so I’ve been upping my intake of fermented foods.

“I avoid using too much ibuprofen and paracetamol if I’m ill. There is some suggestion that ibuprofen isn’t helpful to our immune system and in adults, we don’t always have to lower a fever; it may even be useful in clearing infections. I take 25 micrograms of vitamin D and omega-3 supplements but I am sceptical about other things. What I will have is small amounts of spices, such as a quarter teaspoon of turmeric, cinnamon and some ground cloves in some coconut or almond milk.

highlights.title: Over a Third of Gen Z-ers Rely on AI for Friendship
highlights.summary: Young people who have online-only friends or use AI as a social companion face higher odds of loneliness than those who do not, a new Gallup report reveals.
body: As generational cohorts go, Gen Z has been saddled with its share of labels. They scarcely have sex, are “ quiet quitters ” when it comes to office jobs, and, as they avoid traditional partnership, have learned to solomaxx.
Whether these labels are deserved or completely off the mark, what continually connects this unique class of young people is a desire to reconstruct how they think about connection.

In “ Friendship in an Online-Offline World: Digital Life, Connection and Wellbeing ” researchers from public polling firm Gallup and the Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children’s Hospital found that more than one-third of Gen Z (33 percent) rely on AI for companionship. The percentage was higher among daily AI users, spiking to 50 percent, and 42 percent among those with online-only friends.

highlights.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI, the biggest games release of the decade, is nearly here. Our games editor Keza MacDonald will be online from 4pm to answer all your questions. Ask a question: log in or sign up here.
body: After more than a decade and a reported billion dollars in the making, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally released on Friday. It’s one of the most anticipated games of all time.

The Guardian’s games editor, Keza MacDonald, is one of the first people in the world to have played it. Last month she visited Rockstar North’s headquarters in Edinburgh to go behind the scenes, and she’s now been playing a review copy.

So does it live up to the hype? What’s it like to play as Lucia and Jason, the series’ first double act of protagonists? How big is the new Vice City, and does it really feel alive? And are the radio stations as good as ever?
Keza will be here at 4pm today to answer your questions about the graphics, the open world, the characters, the story and anything else you want to know before you play, without spoilers.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Has A Metacritic Score So High It’s Only Happened Once Before
highlights.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has officially launched, and unsurprisingly, it's earning rave reviews. It's arriving hot on the heels of several critically acclaimed games this year, but does it have enough momentum to knock the current best-reviewed game of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time…
body: When Ocarina of Time launched in early November, it quickly shot to the top of the Metacritic charts, earning a metascore of 96 from GameSpot's sister site. That score came from 128 reviews, and Metacritic rates it as "Universal Acclaim" on its scale. For GTA 6, the game is sitting on a review aggregate of 99 from 98 reviews at the time of writing, with just a single point keeping it away from a perfect score. One thing to note is that Ocarina of Time had more reviews than GTA 6, which affects the review weighting, but overall, both games drew from a broad pool of outlets worldwide.

Don't feel too bad for Ocarina of Time losing its crown, because the only thing better than critical success is commercial success. The remake has sold more than 5 million copies globally in its first four days, and those numbers will keep growing as we enter the festive season. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick recently reacted to the game's release, saying it's "terrific" and that Nintendo has every right to be proud of it.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.title: Helping AI text detectors keep up with changing conditions
highlights.summary: A more flexible training method can make AI text detectors more robust when new models emerge or AI-generated text is disguised to appear human.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

A teacher who believes a student’s term paper may have been written by a large language model (LLM) can use a tool for detecting artificial intelligence-generated text to help confirm their suspicions. But the teacher may want to think twice before putting all their trust in the detector.

Researchers from MIT and Cornell University showed that such detection tools, which are AI models themselves, can be fooled by AI-generated text disguised to appear as if it were written by a human. Detectors can also fail to identify AI text due to natural shifts in writing habits over time or the emergence of new LLMs.
In a new paper, the researchers demonstrated how a special training technique makes an AI detector more accurate and resilient to deception, even as human and AI writing constantly changes.
points: A more flexible training method can make AI text detectors more robust when new models emerge or AI-generated text is disguised to appear human.

Ireland’s fly-half Sam Prendergast is available to face South Africa in the Nations Championship on Saturday after his citing for an alleged hip-drop tackle against Fiji was dismissed.
body: Prendergast was cited for the challenge on Fiji’s captain Peceli Yato under a new offence added to Law 9.13 at the start of November. However, following a hearing on Tuesday, an independent disciplinary committee decided no further action would be taken against the 23-year-old, who could have been hit with a suspension.

South Africa’s head coach Rassie Erasmus had predicted Prendergast would avoid a suspension and be free to play against the Springboks. Erasmus has been handed a six-match ban, which takes immediate effect, after questioning whether the officiating during last Friday’s defeat by France amounted to match-fixing.

A statement from the Nations Championship read: “Sam Prendergast appeared before an independent disciplinary committee on Tuesday 17 November, having been cited for an alleged act of foul play contrary to Law 9.13 during the Nations Championship match between Ireland and Fiji on Saturday 14 November.

body: This isn't just an aspirational goal. It's already happened twice. Luna portrayed Rev-9, an advanced killer robot in Terminator: Dark Fate, and he was an evil arms dealer in the Netflix series FUBAR, both of which starred Schwarzenegger. But in 2026, Luna broke his own rule to take on a very different kind of role: a serial killer.

Luna plays Ray Ballard, aka the Sleepy-Eyed Killer, across two episodes of Dexter: Resurrection season 2. It's a role he was drawn to because of the complex psychology at work within the character, who stalks and kills his victims while they sleep.
"I was fascinated by the psychological warfare he plays with them as he does these home invasions and enters the home for weeks and weeks before he ever culminates the kill," Luna says.

highlights.title: Voyager 1 Beat the Odds and Is Still Working a Light-Day Away From Earth
highlights.summary: The spacecraft stores data on an eight-track tape, but it’s managed to stay in contact with scientists for decades. Now, it’s the first human-made object to travel a light-day away from Earth.
body: One of NASA’s longest-tenured spacecraft is quite literally stuck in the past.

Voyager 1, launched in September 1977 toward the outer planets of our solar system, is poised to achieve a historic milestone on Wednesday: It will be the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth. The spacecraft will be so far away, that by the time its light reaches Earth, it will come from the spacecraft as it existed one day in the past. The achievement is one researchers hadn’t planned on, and yet, as Voyager 1 wades deeper into uncharted stretches of the galaxy, it continues sending back valuable scientific information.

“It's just a wonderful happenstance,” Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, says of the milestone. “Just as the stars were aligned for the tour of the planets, they're also aligned for this really magical, special thing that's happening for humankind.”

Back in the real world, however, on the day when Cameron Bancroft’s 4,000-word mea culpa implicated virtually Australia’s entire touring party back in 2018, the opposite was very much the case. Driven by Ben Duckett’s 115-ball 133, it was England who emerged victorious under lights by a margin of 97 runs.

First came a helter-skelter charge to 328 all out in 48.3 overs, with Duckett’s flurry of 15 fours and three sixes augmented by a critical half-century from Will Jacks at the back end. Then came a charge with the ball similar to Adelaide, culminating in Australia’s collapse to 231 all out on the banks of the Derwent Estuary.

A 2-1 series win for Harry Brook’s tourists, therefore, and a low-key encouraging one, too. Admittedly the hosts were without Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc – a penny for their thoughts right now – but this was still the first time England had come from behind to claim an ODI series in Australia.

But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players.

Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the biggest GTA game to date; it’s also the most romantic. Though the series is well known for its sordid assortment of criminal leads, GTA VI switches things up by starring a pair of thieves who also happen to fall in love after meeting while stealing a car. It’s still an open-world action game full of chaos and mayhem. But many players will also be attempting to nurture the budding relationship in between heists. The sprawling game is designed to support both audiences.

highlights.title: A moment that changed me: the tomato pasta that became an obsession – and helped me lead a better life
highlights.summary: At a restaurant in Italy in 2022, every forkful of my meal made my eyes close and mouth water. For four years since, I have tried to recreate this dish. The pursuit has finally made me a proper vegetarian. I’ve ostensibly been vegetarian for 13 years and, in that time, I’ve eaten a lot of meat.
body: Then I ate a bowl of pasta. It was 2022 and an Italian university friend, Mattia, invited me to Tuscany. I spent four days with his lovely family, in the rolling verdant hills, with fireflies and fallow deer keeping us company, drinking vernaccia and talking of books and art and poetry. But none of that matters, not even a bit. All that matters is a single plate of tomato pasta from Nuova Trattoria Albana, in Mazzolla, west of Siena. This pasta might have seemed, to the untrained palate, like any other pasta. But it changed everything for me.

The pici – handrolled Tuscan pasta, much thicker than spaghetti, a bit thicker than bucatini – was audaciously al dente. The pecorino, sourced from a nearby farm, melted like snow. But the sauce, all’aglione (with garlic), stole the show: the chef’s wife grew tomatoes in the garden next door, picking them fresh every day. Every forkful made my eyes close and my mouth water throughout the meal. If the great object of life is sensation, as Lord Byron suggested, then I’d never felt more alive.

highlights.title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
highlights.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he's AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it.
body: But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous.

Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”

I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.
“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us.”

We already knew Slay the Spire 2 was one of the year's biggest releases. In its first week on sale, the game sold over 3m copies. highlights.summary: Despite pressure from President Trump, Elon Musk, and Silicon Valley executives, Nvidia’s board says it “does not intend” to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO.
body: As Nvidia reported its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, the company’s financial performance was overshadowed by the drama surrounding its former CEO. And Nvidia’s board made one thing clear right off the bat: Jensen Huang isn’t coming back.
At the start of the earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones emphasized the company’s strength and “groundbreaking technology” before turning to the circumstances surrounding Huang’s departure.

“On November 12, our board of directors announced that, after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions … and the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said.

Asked about the company’s strategy for retaining talent and navigating the leadership transition, interim CEO Colette Kress emphasized the importance of the company’s workforce. “Our employees are absolutely instrumental to everything in this company,” Kress said. “We will take care of our employees during this transition to make sure that they are safe and that the work can be done in the current environment.”
points: Despite pressure from President Trump, Elon Musk, and Silicon Valley executives, Nvidia’s board says it “does not intend” to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO.
